messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (about one‑tenth of atmospheric pressure), pure water’s solid–liquid equilibrium lies just below the normal 0 °C freezing point.  
Using the water phase diagram (or standard tables for the melting curve), the melting/freezing temperature at 10 kPa is roughly:

\[
T_{\text{freeze}} \;\approx\; -2^\circ\text{C}
\]

So water would begin to freeze at about –2 °C when the surrounding pressure is 10 kPa.
